sections.domain: Traffic signals, hybrid beacons and sign colors
sections.heading: Traffic signals, hybrid beacons and sign colors
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Traffic signals, hybrid beacons and sign colors

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A40
Reversible-lane signs and signals can change the direction a lane serves at different times of day. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A40
Do not use a lane displaying a red X. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A40
Leave a lane showing a steady yellow X as soon as it is safe because a red X will follow. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A40
A downward-pointing green arrow permits travel in that lane. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A41
A pedestrian hybrid beacon controls a marked crossing at an otherwise unsignalized location. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A41
The text describes a hybrid beacon as two red indications beside each other above a yellow indication. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A41
A hybrid pedestrian-beacon cycle begins with flashing yellow before changing to steady yellow. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A41
The steady-yellow stage of a hybrid beacon carries the meaning of an ordinary yellow signal. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A41
When both hybrid-beacon red lights are steady, drivers stop and remain stopped while pedestrians have WALK. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A41
After WALK ends, the hybrid beacon's red lights alternate while pedestrians receive flashing DON'T WALK. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A41
At alternating red hybrid-beacon lights, stop and confirm that neither your lane nor an adjacent lane contains a pedestrian before proceeding. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A41
A hybrid beacon goes dark after its pedestrian cycle finishes. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A41
The handbook exempts these dark midblock pedestrian beacons from the stop rule applying to a dark traffic signal. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A42
Red sign coloring is associated with stop, yield, do-not-enter and wrong-way messages. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R15 | anchor: A42
Yellow is the warning-sign color for unexpected roadway conditions. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R16 | anchor: A42
Yellow-green warnings identify pedestrian, bicycle, playground, school and school-bus contexts. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R17 | anchor: A42
Pink signs convey incident-management information. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R18 | anchor: A42
Green signs provide guidance such as directions and distances. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R19 | anchor: A42
Blue signs identify motorist services, including rest areas and hospitals. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R20 | anchor: A42
White signs communicate regulatory information such as speed restrictions. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R21 | anchor: A42
Orange signs warn about road workers and construction activity. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R22 | anchor: A42
Brown signs identify recreational and cultural destinations. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> pdf-0042]
